newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel may force out insurance-cartel executives.
newsitem.headline: Israel may force out insurance-cartel executives.

text.p: Israel's insurance commissioner will ask his advisory council next month to rule on whether he can force the resignations of top insurance company executives convicted of running a cartel, the Treasury said on Thursday.

"I am considering using my authority ... to condition the insurance licences of your companies on the basis that anyone convicted of a violation that, in the view of the insurance commissioner, will hurt the credibility of the insurer may not serve and/or continue to serve in a position," commissioner Doron Shorer said in a letter to the companies whose executives were convicted.
The law requires the commissioner to convene a meeting of the council, but a Treasury source termed the process a formality and said Shorer's decision would be affirmed.

Shorer's move is the latest salvo in his battle with the insurers over whether the executives should be forced out. He acted after the justice ministry agreed on May 7 that the law gave him the authority to do so.

The seven companies, among them Israel's largest, were convicted by the Jerusalem District Court of forming a cartel to fix insurance premiums. Among the seven were Migdal, a unit of Leumi Insurance Holdings and Clal Insurance Holdings.
The court imposed fines on the companies and the executives involved, saying they had fixed premiums, coordinated rates and limited discounts in violation of the restrictive business practices law.

The advisory council will meet June 15, Shorer said, and will listen to counter-arguments by the insurance companies. However, a Treasury source said the council was likely to accept Shorer's recommendations.
"Usually the council accepts the view of the commission," the source said, adding however that the companies would almost certainly appeal a decision against them.
